title: What happened in AI — Nov 17, 2026
intro: Coding-agent cost became measurable today. A 27,280-run benchmark found 64% of inference spend went to failed runs and that the best harness depends on the model, while Microsoft's TokenEconomizer trims what agents send per turn.

Around that, the production layer filled in: Datadog now tests agent versions on live traffic, LangSmith restricts trace access, and shared memory and messaging tools (Loom, Woolly, Pulsar) span harnesses. OpenAI shipped GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol.
highlights: 64% of spend in 27,280 coding-agent runs went to failures; re-pick your harness when you switch models.
Datadog Online Experiments compares agent versions on real production traffic, not just eval sets.
LangSmith adds access controls for sensitive data inside agent traces.
ClickHouse's open-source Loom gives coding agents shared code memory (0.78 → 0.84 answer quality).
SageMaker endpoints now route requests to the instance with the longest KV-cache prefix match.
OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol across ChatGPT, Codex, and the API.

categories.name: Coding-agent spend: harness choice decides the bill
categories.summary: Two large measurements say the harness and the context it sends, not just the model, decide what a coding agent costs and whether the money buys a passing run.

articles.title: In 27,280 coding agent runs, 64% of inference spend went to runs that failed
articles.summary: FrontierHarness v1.1 ran 22 harnesses × 5 models × 62 tasks × 4 attempts (83B tokens, with Baseten): 64% of inference spend went to failed runs, and the best harness changes with the model.

articles.title: TokenEconomizer: Learning from Experience to Make AI Coding Agents Efficient
articles.summary: Microsoft Research's TokenEconomizer learns from past sessions which instructions, tool descriptions, and history an agent actually needs, cutting tokens sent per coding-agent turn.

articles.title: NOX Local – a coding agent for 4B models on an 8 GB GPU
articles.summary: NOX Local builds the whole agent loop around a 4B model on llama.cpp and an 8 GB GPU, with MCP, skills, and plan mode, and no API key or per-token bill.

categories.name: Agent memory and multi-agent coordination
categories.summary: Memory and messaging are moving out of individual harnesses into shared, open layers that every coding agent on a machine or team can use.

articles.title: Loom: agent memory that keeps up with your code
articles.summary: ClickHouse open-sourced Loom, a shared code index plus learned-notes store for coding agents; it raised mean answer quality on ClickHouse code questions from 0.78 to 0.84.

articles.title: Show HN: Woolly, a local mem0-compatible memory API for AI agents
articles.summary: Woolly is a local, mem0-compatible memory API that keeps one readable Markdown memory across Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex via SDKs, plugins, and MCP.

articles.title: Show HN: Pulsar – cross-harness agent to agent communication and messaging
articles.summary: Pulsar is an MCP server that puts every local coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and others) on one bus for direct, tagged, or broadcast messages.

articles.title: I Built My Own AI Agent Orchestration Tool
articles.summary: Checkly's Agentic Crafting Table maps 10–20 concurrent coding agents so the operator sees which one needs input instead of polling each session.

articles.title: What We’ve Learned Building Proactive Agents
articles.summary: LangChain's lessons on proactive agents: grant autonomy in stages like a new hire, from scoped tasks to open goals with fewer check-ins.

categories.name: Running agents in production: observability, access, runtimes
categories.summary: Agent platforms are adding the controls platform teams need to run agents at scale: test on live traffic, restrict who sees trace data, and pick the right runtime lifecycle.

articles.title: Datadog Brings Production Experimentation to AI Agent Observability
articles.summary: Datadog Agent Observability adds Online Experiments, comparing agent versions against real production traffic instead of only fixed eval datasets.

articles.title: Protect sensitive data in your traces: new controls in LangSmith
articles.summary: LangSmith adds three controls that limit who can see sensitive data inside production agent traces, so engineers can debug under least-privilege rules.

articles.title: Why Run AI Coding Agents on Kubernetes?
articles.summary: Okteto argues coding agents should move from laptops to Kubernetes once platform teams roll them out to hundreds of developers, for isolation and governance.

articles.title: Not Every Agent Hibernates
articles.summary: Of four common agent patterns, only two ever suspend, so hibernation is not a fleet-wide fix for idle-agent cost; the rest are torn down or run to completion.

categories.name: Inference serving: cache routing and latency budgets
categories.summary: Serving work today targets prompt-cache reuse and tight tail latency, plus a new open runtime for non-NVIDIA silicon.

articles.title: Amazon SageMaker AI real-time endpoints now support KV cache aware routing
articles.summary: SageMaker AI real-time endpoints can now route each request to the instance holding the longest cached prompt match, with guidance on when to prefer prefix-aware routing.

articles.title: Presentation: Scaling LLM-Based Ranking Systems for Latency-Critical Search & Recommendation Workloads
articles.summary: LinkedIn meets P99 SLAs for LLM ranking by distilling 7B to 400M parameters and compressing job context into single-token embeddings for a 10x throughput gain.

articles.title: Show HN: TrnRT – An open-source LLM inference engine for AWS Trainium
articles.summary: RunAnywhere open-sourced TrnRT, an LLM inference engine for AWS Trainium that already serves GLM 5.3 flash in FP8.

categories.name: Models: OpenAI ships GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
categories.summary: OpenAI's 6.2 generation lands across ChatGPT, Codex, and the API, with a vertical legal variant on top.

articles.title: Introducing GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
articles.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, claiming better coding, computer use, and professional output at lower cost in ChatGPT Work, Codex, and the API.

articles.title: Astra for Law leads in legal intelligence
articles.summary: Astra for Law ranked first in OpenAI's launch evaluation across 24 areas of law; ChatGPT Enterprise customers can request access.

articles.title: CLI for torrenting open weight AI models
articles.summary: Pirate Face CLI fetches 37,160 open-weight models over BitTorrent and falls back to Hugging Face, so a stalled 15 GB CI download no longer fails the job.
